title: 第八百五十一章 深度，－1——致新世界
content_zh:
第八百五十一章深度，1——致新世界第八百五十一章深度，1——致新世界
然后，便有了光。
而那已经是很久很久以前的事情了——亦可能是一瞬间前的事情。
毕竟，如果阿尔格莱德的占星师们理论正确，这个宇宙的诞生很可能只是前不久才发生的事情——尽管对于宇宙中众生的时间标尺而言，那可能已经是“亿万年之前的事件”，但对于另一个高于宇宙万物的时间标尺而言，亿万年的时间跨度只是一个无足轻重的参数。
可谁又会在意呢？反正一个整日里要忙着完成自己的生物学毕业论文、每天睡眠时间已经压缩到不足六个小时的大四学废肯定不会在意这种“天上的事情”——隔壁的天文会可能在意，那是另一码事，他们的学分跟这个挂钩。
博尔诺抱着一大摞刚刚从图书馆里借来的资料，脚步匆匆地跑过学院都市顶层的大步道，身后仿佛能带起一阵狂风。
他从一位头发乱糟糟的、仿佛严重缺乏睡眠的精灵先生身旁跑过去，险些撞到了对方。
“不准在上层步道奔跑！”头发乱糟糟的精灵先生踉跄了一下，高声提醒着这个不知道从哪冒出来的矮个子小伙——从身体尺寸和那特征鲜明的、猫科动物一般的耳朵判断，这应该是个吉普洛族的学生，这个种族总是这样冒冒失失的。
“对不起先生！”博尔诺慌忙停下，转身，以一种几乎要把怀里的一摞书扔在对面先生身上的姿势猛地弯腰致歉，“我急着去见我的导师——我在图书馆耽搁太久，抬头一看表才发现已经迟到快半个小时了！非常抱歉，没伤到您吧？”
吉普洛小伙子的诚恳与紧张态度发挥了作用，精灵先生有些无奈地摆了摆手：“好吧，你赶快去吧，放导师的鸽子可不是小事——但是不要再这样横冲直撞了，世界不会因为你跑得慢了一点就毁灭掉。”
“是……谢谢先生！再见先生！我走了先生！”
博尔诺连连鞠躬，又手忙脚乱地接住了就要从怀里滑出去的书本，这才转过身，快步朝大步道的另一头走去。
头发乱糟糟、因为缺乏睡眠而带着黑眼圈的精灵男性则看着冒冒失失跑远的年轻人，有些无奈地摇了摇头。
脚步声从旁边传来，他抬头看向声音传来的方向，看到一个熟悉的身影不知何时已经来到附近，他脸上露出一丝笑容，抬手与对方打着招呼：“泰德，真难得看到你在这个时候有空闲出来散步。”
“更难得看到你这家伙愿意从自己的实验室里出来，呼吸外面的空气，”泰德·里尔看了面前的精灵大学者一眼，随口调侃道，“你不是说精灵每天只需要摄取基本的维生物质并保持每天十五分钟的光照和两分钟户外活动就可以维持生命体征了吗？”
“我是这么认为的——但我的医生不这么想，”塔兰·艾尔耸耸肩，“他把我从实验室里轰出来了。”
“……轰的好，”泰德·里尔翻了个白眼，“你这身体如果没人盯着，活不过两千岁就得英年早逝——说真的，世界这么好，你就不想多活些年，好好看看这个世界再死？非得作啊？”
听着多年好友这丝毫不客气的调侃和教训，塔兰·艾尔只是讪讪地笑了笑，无从反驳地摸了摸自己的鼻子。
“是啊……这么好……”
他小声嘀咕着，又慢慢抬起头，眺望着大步道的尽头，目光越过了学院高塔的尖顶，越过那些高墙，越过城市外面的广袤平原与丘陵，看向地平线的方向。

有壮丽如山脉般的绿色在大地上连绵起伏，庞大的树影伫立在地平线尽头，而从那树冠顶层逸散出的浅绿幻光则仿若极光般弥漫于天空，又化作光河流向平原，绿意如脉，在大地上蜿蜒流淌，有的流于地表，有的则渗入地下，消失在某些支流的尽头。
那些被称作“洛卡之触”的能量流一直深入地下很深很深的地方，并在地幔附近交织成为更加巨大的网络，在地壳和地幔之间包裹着整个星球——而能量流所到的地方，皆是席兰蒂斯的祝福之处。
这座“学园都市”，便建立在轻风平原上最大的一处能量焦点上。
但实际上这些“能量焦点”对于城市本身的运转而言并没什么用——城市运行需要的是电力和燃料，地下深处的能量焦点唯一的作用就是让精灵们能够和席兰蒂斯建立更直接的交流。
席兰蒂斯喜欢跟人聊天——萨斯洛卡也喜欢，在巡行间隙的时候，祂也会在线上。
塔兰·艾尔眯起眼睛，明媚的阳光洒在他的脸上，带着一种让人忍不住困倦的温暖热量。
“你听说那件事了吗？”泰德·里尔的声音从旁边传来，将塔兰·艾尔从昏昏欲睡中唤醒，“阿尔格莱德的占星师们——他们了解到了一些不得了的情况。”
“……交界地那边总是有各种各样的情报流通，泰拉和交界地之间又有着长期稳定的交流，更何况……阿尔格莱德人本就是一个对群星很敏锐的种族，”塔兰·艾尔不紧不慢地说道，“我认为这并不是什么大问题——如果世界是这样，那它就应该是这样，既然他们察觉了，那就让他们知道吧，毕竟……还有那么多同样敏锐和智慧的种族，生活在如此广袤无垠的星空深处，而我们能触及到和影响到的，永远只是其中最最小的一部分……”
大学者说着，在阳光中慢慢伸了个懒腰，仿佛要把这阳光也吸进肺中一般深深地吸了口气，又慢慢将气吐出。
“泰德，别想那么多了，像我一样享受这空气与微风吧，还有温暖的阳光……说真的，我真开始有点喜欢户外了，原来晒太阳是这么好的一件事情。”
泰德·里尔看了塔兰一眼，随后也仿佛突然放松了下来，他笑着摇了摇头，也学着塔兰那样眯起眼睛，让温暖的阳光照在脸上。
但是只过了一会，他又仿佛突然想起什么，忍不住小声嘀咕道：“话又说回来了，伱觉得‘他’对这事儿会是怎么个看法？群星中有原生的智慧生灵开始自发地察觉到这个世界诞生过程中的某些奥秘……”
塔兰·艾尔耸耸肩：“他？他没什么看法。”
“……你怎么知道？”
“上次露克蕾西亚女士回来的时候跟我说的——‘他’现在要忙的事情可是一大堆，而对于群星间的原生智慧生灵在发展过程中出现的各种情况……‘他’只秉承一个原则：只要别把房掀了，就不管。”
“……是不是过于心宽了点？”
“谁知道呢？”塔兰·艾尔随口说道，“有句话怎么说的来着……哦，尽最大努力确保这个世界所拥有的‘可能性’，大概是这个意思。”
泰德·里尔想了想，觉得这里面有着很深奥且极具说服力的道理，便决定不在这个话题上纠结下去，只是略有些好奇地问了一句：“你知道‘他’现在在忙什么吗？”
“那我就更不知道了，反正……这么大的地方，他要忙的事情肯定不少。”
塔兰·艾尔说着，抬头看向了遥远的天空。

他仿佛注视着一个无尽遥远的地方——那是星球之外，是星系之外，在空间与时间的涟漪夹缝，在某种已经超出人智能够理解的、无尽的时空结构深处。
他仅仅在少数几次经过引导的幻象中短暂地重新拜访过那个地方。
拜访过那艘船。
那在巴摩萨人最古老晦涩的传说中，“古圣灵”们聚会的地方——
“情况，就是这么个情况，”身材高大的凡娜起身——在星空深处的某些故事中，她又被称作“执剑圣女”，或“击落星辰者”、“坠星女士”——一脸严肃地说道，“稍微有点棘手，可能得咱们亲自去一趟了。”
长桌尽头那个高大威严的身影沉默着没有开口，而桌子对面的雪莉已经抱着脑袋趴了下来——不知从什么时候开始，她被巴摩萨人称作了“巡视天空的女士”或“掷星者”：“可是我昨天刚刚刚刚刚放假啊！”
“总得救吧，”坐在长桌一角的“双子星辰”、“镜中保护者”阿加莎（影）摇了摇头，“好歹也算是船上的……”
“这事儿别传出去就行，”莫里斯叼着烟斗，看了一眼长桌尽头的高大身影——他的称号实在太多，有时候连他自己都不记得——表情有些微妙地说着，“主要是别传到利维坦们那边去，他们都抗议过三次了……”
长桌尽头的高大身影终于动弹了一下，于是桌子两边的讨论声终于稍稍安静下来。
一道道目光都带着期待落在了船长身上。
那身影从黑暗中起身——邓肯周铭环视着聚集在这里的追随者们，面色复杂地沉默良久之后终于发出一声叹息，神色渐渐抓狂：
“所以，谁能首先解释一下，‘旅行中的蕾·诺拉忽悠着跷家的利维坦女王跑去欣赏宇宙大呲花结果双双被引力坍塌卡进了空间裂缝里只好发来求救信号找人帮忙把她俩扣出来’到底是怎么个意思——然后再简要解释一下，为什么是第四次？！前三次又是怎么回事？！”
一旁的妮娜顿时抬头小心翼翼地四周看了看，嘀嘀咕咕：“不先解释一下什么是宇宙大呲花吗？听着很有意思哎……”
妮娜话音刚落，桌子上放着的山羊头顿时仰起脖子，语气特兴奋：“哎这个我知道，上次巡视任务的时候我去看了，就是类星体遇上……”
它这话刚说个开头，桌子周围的所有人顿时异口同声：“闭嘴！”
“……哦。”
（大结局）
深度失乡号仍在远航。）

Chapter 851 Depth, 1——To a new world Chapter 851 Depth, 1——To a new world
Then, there was light.
And that was a long, long time ago—or maybe a moment ago.
After all, if the theory of the astrologers in Algrade is correct, the birth of this universe is likely to have happened not long ago - although for the time scale of all living beings in the universe, it may have been an "event hundreds of millions of years ago", but for another time scale higher than all things in the universe, the time span of billions of years is just an insignificant parameter.
But who cares? Anyway, a college senior who is busy finishing his biology graduation thesis all day long and whose sleep time has been reduced to less than six hours a day will definitely not care about such "heavenly things" - the astronomy club next door may care, but that is another matter, their credits are linked to this.
Borno held a large pile of materials he had just borrowed from the library and ran hurriedly across the large walkway on the top floor of Academy City, as if he could bring a strong wind behind him.
He ran past an elf gentleman with messy hair who seemed to be severely sleep deprived, and almost bumped into him.
"No running on the upper walkway!" Mr. Elf with messy hair staggered and loudly reminded this short guy who appeared out of nowhere - judging from the body size and the distinctive, feline-like ears, this should be a student of the Gipulo tribe. This race is always so reckless.
"I'm sorry, sir!" Borno stopped in a hurry, turned around, and apologized by bending down in a posture that almost threw the stack of books in his arms on the gentleman opposite him. "I was in a hurry to see my tutor - I was delayed in the library for too long, and when I looked up at my watch, I realized that I was almost half an hour late! I'm very sorry. Didn't I hurt you?"
The sincerity and nervous attitude of the young man Jipulo came into play, and Mr. Elf waved his hand helplessly: "Okay, go ahead and let go of the mentor's doves is not a trivial matter - but don't run rampant like this anymore, the world will not be destroyed just because you run a little slower."
"Yes...thank you sir! Goodbye sir! I'm leaving sir!"
Borno bowed repeatedly and hurriedly caught the book that was about to slip out of his arms. Then he turned around and walked quickly towards the other end of the long walk.
The elf male with messy hair and dark circles under his eyes due to lack of sleep looked at the young man who ran away recklessly and shook his head helplessly.
The sound of footsteps came from the side. He looked up in the direction of the sound and saw a familiar figure arriving nearby. A smile appeared on his face and he raised his hand to say hello: "Ted, it's rare to see you free for a walk at this time."
"It's even rarer to see a guy like you willing to come out of your laboratory and breathe the outside air," Ted Leal glanced at the elf scholar in front of him and joked casually, "Didn't you say that elves only need to take in basic vitamins every day and maintain fifteen minutes of light and two minutes of outdoor activities to maintain vital signs?"
“I thought so—but my doctor didn’t,” shrugged Taran Ayre. “He kicked me out of the lab.”
"...That's great," Ted Leal rolled his eyes, "If no one is watching your body, you will die young if you don't live to be more than two thousand years old - seriously, the world is so good, don't you want to live a few more years and take a good look at the world before you die? Do you have to do it?"
Listening to the unceremonious teasing and lessons from his long-time friend, Taran Ayre just smiled and touched his nose without being able to refute.
"Yeah...so good..."
He murmured quietly and slowly raised his head again,Looking at the end of the big trail, he looked past the spiers of the college tower, past the high walls, past the vast plains and hills outside the city, and towards the horizon.
There are magnificent mountains of green rolling across the land, with huge tree shadows standing at the end of the horizon, and the light green phantom light escaping from the top of the tree canopy fills the sky like an aurora, and turns into a river of light flowing to the plains. The green veins meander on the earth, some flowing on the surface, and some seeping into the ground and disappearing at the end of some tributaries.
Those energy flows called "Lorca's Touch" go deep into the ground, and intertwine into a larger network near the mantle, wrapping the entire planet between the crust and the mantle - and wherever the energy flows go, they are all places blessed by Selantis.
This "Academy City" is built on the largest energy focus on the Qingfeng Plain.
But in fact, these "energy focus" are of little use to the operation of the city itself - the city requires electricity and fuel to operate, and the only function of the energy focus deep underground is to allow the elves to establish more direct communication with Silantis.
Silantis loved chatting with people—and so did Saslokar, who was also online during breaks in tours.
Taran El squinted his eyes, and the bright sunlight shone on his face, bringing with it a kind of warmth that made people unable to help but feel sleepy.
"Did you hear about that?" Ted Leal's voice came from the side, waking Taran El from his drowsiness. "The astrologers in Algrade - they learned about something terrible."
"... There is always a variety of information flowing over the border, and there are long-term and stable exchanges between Terra and the border. What's more... the Algradians are a race that is very sensitive to the stars," Taran Ayre said unhurriedly, "I don't think this is a big problem - if If the world is like this, then it should be like this. Now that they are aware of it, let them know. After all... there are so many equally keen and intelligent races living in the depths of such a vast and boundless starry sky, and what we can touch and influence is always only the smallest part of it..."
As the scholar spoke, he slowly stretched out in the sunshine, took a deep breath as if he wanted to suck the sunshine into his lungs, and then slowly exhaled.
"Ted, don't think so much. Just enjoy the air, the breeze, and the warm sunshine like I do... To be honest, I really started to like the outdoors. It turns out that basking in the sun is such a good thing."
Ted Leal glanced at Taran, and then seemed to suddenly relax. He smiled and shook his head, and imitated Taran and squinted his eyes to let the warm sunshine shine on his face.
But after a while, he seemed to suddenly remember something, and couldn't help but murmur in a low voice: "Then again, what do you think 'he' would think about this matter? There are native intelligent beings among the stars who have begun to spontaneously notice certain mysteries in the birth process of this world..."
Taran Ayre shrugged: "Him? He doesn't have any opinions."
"...How do you know?"
"Ms. Lucretia told me when she came back last time - 'he' has a lot of things to be busy with now, and regarding the various situations that arise in the development process of the native intelligent beings among the stars... 'he' only adheres to one principle: as long as the house is not overturned, it doesn't matter."
"...Are you being too lenient?"
"Who knows?" Taran El said casually, "There is a saying... Oh, try your best to ensure the 'possibility' that this world has, that's probably what it means."
Ted Leal thought about it and felt that there was a very profound and convincing truth in it, so he decidedWithout dwelling on this topic, I just asked with some curiosity: "Do you know what 'he' is busy with now?"
"Then I don't know. Anyway... in such a big place, he must be busy with a lot of things."
Taran El said, looking up at the distant sky.
He seemed to be staring at an infinitely distant place - that was outside the planet, outside the galaxy, between the ripples of space and time, deep in some endless space-time structure that was beyond the comprehension of human intelligence.
He only briefly revisited the place in a few guided visions.
Visited that ship.
In the oldest and obscure legend of the Bamosa people, the place where the "ancient holy spirits" gather -
"This is the situation," the tall Fanna stood up - in some stories in the depths of the starry sky, she is also known as the "Sword-wielding Saint", or "The Star-Downer", or the "Falling Star Lady" - said with a serious face, "It's a little tricky, we may have to go there in person."
The tall and majestic figure at the end of the long table was silent and did not speak, while Shirley across the table had already laid down with her head in her arms - I don't know since when, she was called "the lady who patrols the sky" or "the star thrower" by the Bamosa people: "But I just had a holiday yesterday!"
"It must be saved," Agatha (Shadow), the "Twin Stars" and "Protector in the Mirror" sitting at the corner of the long table, shook her head, "I am still on the ship after all..."
"Just don't spread this matter," Morris held his pipe in his mouth and glanced at the tall figure at the end of the long table - he had so many titles that sometimes even he himself couldn't remember - and said with a subtle expression, "The main thing is don't spread it to the Leviathans. They have protested three times..."
The tall figure at the end of the long table finally moved, and the discussion on both sides of the table finally quieted down a little.
All eyes fell on the captain with expectation.
The figure stood up from the darkness - Duncan Zhou Ming looked around at the followers gathered here, with a complex expression on his face. After a long silence, he finally let out a sigh, his expression gradually going crazy:
"So, who can first explain what it means, 'Lei Nora, who was traveling, deceived Queen Leviathan of the wandering family to go to admire the giant flowers of the universe, but they were both trapped in the space crack by the collapse of gravity, and had to send a distress signal to find someone to help pull them out.' - and then briefly explain, why is it the fourth time?! What happened the first three times?!"
Nina on the side immediately raised her head and looked around cautiously, muttering: "Why don't you explain what the cosmic giant flower is first? It sounds very interesting..."
As soon as Nina finished speaking, the goat head on the table suddenly raised its neck and said in a very excited tone: "Hey, I know this. I went to see it during the last inspection mission, which was about Quasar Encounter..."
As soon as it started to say this, everyone around the table suddenly said in unison: "Shut up!"
"...Oh."
(finale)
The Deep Lost Home is still on its voyage. )
